title: Universal Improvement of Channel Fidelity via Entanglement Assistance
abstract: Communication using quantum channels generally requires encoding and decoding on many identical uses of a quantum channel. In practical settings, decoherence may severely limit our ability to do so, potentially rendering each channel use nonidentical. Given $n$ nonidentical channels, we present an entanglement-assisted encoding and decoding strategy that yields a channel with higher worst-case fidelity than all of the $n$ given channels. The strategy is universal, in the sense that the improvement holds regardless of what channels are given, as long as they satisfy mild assumptions on their initial entanglement fidelities. Our protocol is optimal when the given channels are depolarizing channels, and is essentially the unique one that is universal. This idea can also be extended to classical channels, where shared randomness between the sender and the receiver allows universal enhancement of the probability of correct transmission. We then consider general quantum resource theories, providing a necessary condition and a sufficient condition for the possibility of such universal improvement of quantum resources.
summary: This paper introduces a universal, entanglement-assisted protocol to boost the worst-case fidelity of quantum channels when multiple noisy channels are available. By constructing a specific superinstrument, the authors demonstrate that the output channel can surpass the fidelity of any individual input channel. This establishes a powerful theoretical tool for quantum communication resource enhancement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of finding a universal method to improve the worst-case fidelity of quantum communication channels when multiple, potentially non-identical channels are used.
main_result: It proves that an entanglement-assisted encoding and decoding strategy can universally enhance the worst-case fidelity of quantum channels beyond the fidelity of any single given channel.
method: The authors employ resource theory concepts, constructing an entanglement-assisted superinstrument ($\Theta$) acting on the tensor product of the input channels to achieve the enhancement.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum communication using $n$ nonidentical quantum channels $\{N_i\}$. The analysis is framed using superchannels and resource theories, particularly focusing on fidelity measures.
key_observables: Worst-case fidelity ($F(N)$) and entanglement fidelity ($	ext{Fe}(	ext{N})$) are the primary observables used to quantify channel quality.
important_parameters: The number of channels ($n$), the initial entanglement fidelities of the channels, and the critical fidelity threshold ($F_c$) are important parameters.
main_assumptions: The protocol requires the input channels to satisfy mild assumptions on their initial entanglement fidelities, and the analysis often relies on the ability to perform channel twirling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical decomposition of superchannels and superinstruments, and show the general task of achieving universal channel fidelity improvement.
paper_structure: The paper develops the problem by defining the goal of universal fidelity improvement, constructs the entanglement-assisted protocol, proves its optimality for specific channels (like depolarizing ones), and then generalizes the findings to classical channels and general resource theories.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental theoretical tools for understanding how shared quantum resources (like entanglement) can overcome inherent noise limitations in communication protocols, which is central to quantum networking.
